Connect Android Auto to the car browser
This guide takes about two minutes. Prepare Android Auto, connect the car to this phone hotspot, start NavOnWeb, then pair the browser.
Do every setup step while safely parked. Do not operate the phone or vehicle display while driving.
1. Start Android Auto Head Unit Server

Search for Android Auto in phone settings. Near the bottom, tap Version and then tap Version and permission info 10 times to enable developer mode. Open the top-right overflow menu and tap Start head unit server. If Stop head unit server is shown, it is already running.
A phone restart or Android Auto update may stop this developer server. Start it again before using NavOnWeb.
Open Android Auto settings
2. Connect the viewing device to this phone hotspot
Turn on Mobile Hotspot in phone Settings. In the viewing device’s Wi-Fi menu, select this hotspot and enter its password.

NavOnWeb video travels directly over the local connection between the phone and viewing device, so the video stream itself does not use the phone’s mobile data. Opening navonweb.com and setting up the connection may use a small amount of internet data. Diagnostics or service traffic, map or software updates, and music or video streaming from the viewing device can also use mobile data. Check the data allowance and automatic update or streaming settings first.
3. Start NavOnWeb
Return to NavOnWeb and tap Start service. Review any notification or approximate-location permission request. Wait until Android Auto shows Connected and a browser address appears.
4. Pair a web browser

On the device where you want to view the screen, open https://navonweb.com in a web browser. Enter the 8-digit registration code shown in NavOnWeb. The approved browser is remembered for later connections.
If connection is unavailable for more than 10 seconds, use Get a new pairing code in the browser, issue a fresh code in the phone app, and enter it again.
